author: independent instrument-review lane
role: The independent leg IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 7.8 names. This artifact reviews TWO INSTRUMENTS, not the artifacts they check. Both subjects were independently reviewed ACCEPT with 0 blockers and neither of those verdicts is reopened, revisited or relied upon here.
binds: This artifact binds NOTHING. It changes no status, disposition, verdict or seal, closes no row, repoints no head, applies nothing and authorises nothing. CD-RT-5 remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A. TM remains UNSET - BLOCKS FREEZE. The two instruments and their two subjects are byte-identical to the bytes reviewed, re-measured at the end of this run.
verdictMeaning: Both instruments are real, re-runnable measurements that can fail the build, and section 7.8's central ruling -- that a companion instrument converts an unverifiable attestation into a re-runnable check and converts neither into independent evidence -- is CONFIRMED by measurement rather than accepted on assertion. Two blockers are raised against the INSTRUMENTS' coverage, not against their subjects: in each case something checkable is neither checked nor disclosed, and in each case a green run therefore means materially less than its banner reads.

blockers.title: The seventeen published vectors are never required to differ. Ten of them can be collapsed into digest-identical duplicates of PDD-01 and the instrument reports 0 findings.
blockers.whatIsClaimed: PDD-05..PDD-15 are published by the subject as SYNTHETIC INCLUSION CONTROLS -- each one's stated meaning is that it differs from PDD-01 in exactly one field and therefore produces a different derivationDigest. PDD-16 is an ordering-axis control and PDD-17 is the ordering trap.
blockers.whatIsMeasured: The instrument recomputes every published digest FROM the published recordValue, which is genuine arithmetic. It never checks that two vectors differ. Setting a control's recordValue to PDD-01's recordValue and republishing the digests with the instrument's own encoder yields a corpus in which two published vectors carry ONE identical derivationDigest, and the instrument returns 0 findings.

measurement.technique: mutate a copy of the subject, republish recordBytes / recordSha256 / leafRootHex / outerPreimageHex / derivationDigest / completeRecordHex with the instrument's own encode_a, then feed the result back through the instrument's own --subject entry point
measurement.note: PDD-05 could not be neutralised in place because encoder A independently refuses variant=completed with a deficiency field -- a real guard, correctly firing -- but PDD-05 DOES collapse fully.

blockers.whyItIsABlocker: The instrument enumerates 720 SYNTHETIC values and requires 720 distinct encodings with 0 collisions. It applies no distinctness requirement at all to the 17 PUBLISHED vectors it presents to a reader as controls. The distinctness discipline is applied to the corpus nobody reads and withheld from the corpus everybody reads. A signer reading the banner line '17 vectors recomputed on every published field by TWO independent encoders, 0 disagreements' will reasonably conclude the vector corpus is sound; it can be nine-tenths duplicates.
blockers.notDisclosed: NOT_VERIFIED lists five items and none of them is this. This is checkable in a handful of lines -- assert len({v.derivationDigest}) == 17, and assert each control differs from PDD-01 in exactly the field it names -- so it is not a limitation that had to be filed as unverifiable. It is simply absent.
blockers.whatWouldClearIt: Require pairwise distinctness of derivationDigest across the 17 published vectors, and require each inclusion control to differ from PDD-01 in exactly the field its `models` string names and in no other. Both are mechanical and neither needs anything outside the artifact.
blockers.scope: Raised against the INSTRUMENT's coverage. It is not a finding against r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.6.json, whose live bytes carry 17 genuinely distinct vectors -- verified this run. No status changes.

blockers.title: Required-substring binding is defeated by text that contains every required substring and then reverses it. 63 bound positions fall, including all five property statements.
blockers.whatIsClaimed: The instrument replaces the six INSUFFICIENT assertions its subject specified with roughly 70 required substrings across 24 positions, and proves non-vacuity by showing that a rootBinding gutted to placeholders loses every needle and is rejected at every position.
blockers.whatIsMeasured: require_substrings tests `needle not in text` with no negation, retraction or contradiction detection, and text_of flattens a list or dict position by joining it. A successor that keeps every required substring verbatim and appends a retraction passes silently. This is not a hypothetical: 13 of 13 hand-written substring-preserving negations escaped, and a full sweep of the effective contract puts the boundary at 63 positions.

measurement.negationHoleDefinition: positions the instrument DOES bind by containment (replacing the leaf is caught) but where preserving every needle and appending a reversal is NOT caught

representativeEscapes: properties.SN-P1.statement -- keeps 'total function of exactly one input' and 'argument position by which a root may be supplied', then adds that a host MAY accept a caller-supplied root as an additional argument and the resolver is NOT a total function of one input
properties.SN-P1.dispositiveVersusAdvisory -- keeps 'activeRootId is dispositive', then withdraws it and makes activeRootCanonicalPath dispositive instead
properties.SN-P2.statement -- keeps 'activeRootId -> activeRootCanonicalPath is a FUNCTION', then downgrades it to advisory and permits two live records at two locators
properties.SN-P3.statement -- keeps 'STORAGE_ROOT_NOT_ONE_DEVICE before any user-derived durable write', then exempts the check until after the first such write and tolerates mount points in scope
properties.SN-P4.ordering -- keeps 'The record precedes the namespace', then inverts the ordering
properties.SN-P5.statement -- keeps 'migration install rename onto a target the journal already reserved', then permits it and silently overwrites

observabilityBoundary.rule -- keeps 'release-gated under G14' and 'no instrument in this corpus can observe it', then claims this instrument DOES observe runtime conformance and the G14 gate is discharged
fixtures.enforcementDisclosure -- keeps 'check-threat-claims.py' and 'not a regression instrument', then asserts the vectors are in fact ENFORCED and need no successor work
blockers.sharpestForm: The instrument's OWN mutation list contains _paper_seal_the_disclosure, which replaces fixtures.enforcementDisclosure wholesale with 'These vectors are enforced.' and is correctly rejected as SNV4-P0. The same paper seal, written so as to keep the original sentence and append the contradiction, escapes. The instrument catches the lazy form of an attack it has already named and misses the careful form of the same attack.
blockers.whyItIsABlocker: The five property statements are the entire substantive content the instrument was written to bind -- SNV4R-NB-03 exists precisely because a checker carrying only the six specified assertions 'would pass on a rootBinding gutted to placeholders'. The repair closes gutting and leaves reversal open. Against an author who is careless the binding holds; against an author who is careful it does not, and a successor is written by someone who has read the checker.
blockers.notDisclosed: The word negation, contradiction, reword, rephrase and brittle do not occur anywhere in the instrument's 104473 bytes (whitespace-normalised search). The corpus already knows this attack: versioning-policy.v10.json, using the same technique, publishes the quantified boundary at successorRevision.evidenceEnforcementRepair.retainedResiduals[0].measured -- 'An edit to the free prose AROUND the required substrings is NOT caught. Measured boundary: across the 340 string leaves in the two partitioned scopes, appending a false sentence while preserving every required measured substring is admitted at 80 of them.' The namespace instrument neither defends against the class nor carries the disclosure a sibling lane had already written.
blockers.whatWouldClearIt: Either (a) carry the disclosure with the quantified boundary, as versioning-policy.v10 does, so a reader knows what the green run does not cover; or (b) bind the load-bearing positions by exact equality or by a length/edit budget in addition to containment, accepting the reword-brittleness that R-1 already accepts at its own bound positions. (a) is honest and cheap; (b) is stronger and costs false positives.
blockers.scope: Raised against the INSTRUMENT's coverage. It is not a finding against threat-model-storage-namespace.v4.json, whose live prose says what it should -- verified this run. No status changes.

perInstrument.subject: artifacts/threat-model-storage-namespace.v4.json
perInstrument.evidenceCategory: (b) re-runnable author-side evidence, with its prose half at (c)
perInstrument.evidenceCategoryReasoning: This instrument has two halves and they earn different grades. The COMPUTED half is the strongest work in either instrument: it decides outcomes from worlds using a resolver written in the checker that HAS NO ROOT PARAMETER -- the property expressed as code rather than as prose -- re-derives rename operand pairs from layout, and counts recovery-table closure with len() and hard-compares against the prose counts. I attacked it 141 ways and it did not yield once. That half is (b) and locally reaches toward (a), because re-deriving a value from the layout is not the same act as reading the value back. The PROSE half is (c): it tests that the subject's sentences contain substrings the checker also contains, which is agreement between two statements of one reading, and CIR-B2 shows the agreement survives the reading being reversed. Since SN-P1..SN-P5 ARE the artifact's substance, the instrument as a whole cannot be graded above (b), and a signer must not read the green run as covering the meaning of the five properties.
perInstrument.whatWouldMoveItUp: To reach (a) the five properties would have to be re-derived rather than re-stated -- for example by an independent lane writing its own decider for SN-P1..SN-P5 from the reviewed semantics and requiring the artifact's prose to be consistent with THAT, the way SNV4-V already decides the six vectors from worlds. The instrument proves this is possible: it does exactly that for the vectors, the operand pairs and the recovery closure. Extending the technique from the fixtures to the properties is the move from (c) to (b) for the prose half. Nothing short of a second lane re-deriving the properties reaches (a).

nonVacuityReproduced.rootBindingGuttedNote: 133 REPRODUCES, but only under one gutting definition: recursive replacement of every string leaf with a placeholder while PRESERVING list structure. Sweep of 24 gutting definitions attached at nonBlockingObservations CIR-NB-02.
nonVacuityReproduced.perPropertyGuttedNote: measured range is 5-18, NOT the 13-18 section 7.8 records. Stable across every gutting definition tested and across keeping or discarding `title`. See CIR-NB-01.
nonVacuityReproduced.duplicateKeyProbe: rejected, naming both the key and its path

pinAndSemanticsFireSeparately.claim: written to disk, gutted bytes are refused at exit 2 on digest drift, while a re-pinned scratch copy produces findings
pinAndSemanticsFireSeparately.method: built a sandbox tree with the data files symlinked and the two __file__-resolving Python files copied, so ROOT resolves inside the sandbox; wrote gutted bytes over the subject; ran the SHIPPED checker; then re-pinned a SCRATCH COPY of the checker to the mutated digest and re-ran. Re-pinning a scratch copy of the checker is the technique both instrument authors used and I used it here; no repository file was edited.
pinAndSemanticsFireSeparately.shippedCheckerStderr: DIGEST DRIFT on artifacts/threat-model-storage-namespace.v4.json ... This checker scores the bytes it was reviewed against and refuses to score any others.
pinAndSemanticsFireSeparately.ruling: The mechanism is real and the two guards are genuinely independent. This IS the right standard for non-vacuity -- driving the shipped file from outside itself defeats the failure mode where a selftest and the code under test share a bug -- and I endorse it. It is necessary and it is not sufficient: it proves the assertions fire on ABSENCE. CIR-B2 is the demonstration that firing on absence and firing on falsehood are different properties, and this standard measures only the first.

computedNotQuoted.recoveryClosure: purge 6 rows and migration 10 rows are counted with len() and hard-compared against the counts written in prose; duplicating a row is caught as 'records purge at 6 rows, live table measures 7', and retargeting a nextState to a nonexistent state is caught
computedNotQuoted.ruling: genuinely computed. 141 substitutions across three families, zero escapes.

computedObservationVerified.claim: the control/ scan-depth bound is reported by READING depth off layout.purgeJournal and parsing the recursion grant out of SN-P3's own clause, rather than by quoting
evidence: baseline reports purgeJournal sits 2 directory levels below control/
moving purgeJournal one level shallower re-reports 0
moving it three levels deep re-reports 3
moving it out of control/ switches to the third branch: 'does not sit beneath <admittedStorageRoot>/control/, so the measurement does not apply to these bytes and is not reported'

computedObservationVerified.ruling: This is computed, not quoted, and it WOULD report differently if a successor disclosed or granted the bound -- both branches exercised. It is the single best-engineered observation I found in either instrument: it carries a review finding forward mechanically and retires itself when the finding is repaired, in either of the two ways it could be repaired. It also correctly reports that the operand set is fully covered, so the blocker IS repaired and only the disclosure is missing.

whatItDeclinesToVerify.declared: runtime conformance is recorded as G14-class and unobservable: whether a built host honours SN-P1..SN-P5 is not observable from a specification by any instrument in this corpus
whatItDeclinesToVerify.honestyReasoning: Correct and correctly scoped. A specification-level instrument cannot observe a host, and SNV4-OBS-UNENFORCED-ELSEWHERE says so in the banner and adds that nothing here clears the TM row. SNV4-OBS-DISCLOSURE-SCOPE is also accurate: T13's closed-set equality over storageNamespace.fixtures would still reject an addition there, so the enforcement disclosure remains true of that checker.
whatItDeclinesToVerify.incompletenessReasoning: The list is honest about what is UNOBSERVABLE and silent about what is merely UNCHECKED. The negation hole (CIR-B2) is a specification-level property, fully checkable, neither checked nor disclosed. Nothing checkable is misfiled AS unverifiable -- the G14 boundary is drawn in the right place -- but the boundary between 'bound' and 'not bound' inside the specification level is not drawn at all.

freezeComplianceInTheInstrumentItself.section75DuplicateKeyNamesTheKey: EXCEEDS. jloads records every repeated key AGAINST ITS OWN PATH and reports it as a named finding at that position rather than raising, so an operator is told where to look. It also handles the two hard cases: duplicates sitting in an object the parse itself discarded are refused with a count even though their path cannot be resolved, and a live reference to every recording object is retained so no id() can be reused by a collected object while paths are resolved. That id()-reuse hazard is real and is the kind of thing most implementations get wrong.
freezeComplianceInTheInstrumentItself.section6Law18ExactType: COMPLIANT. jtype() tests isinstance(value, bool) BEFORE isinstance(value, int), which is exactly the required bool-before-int ordering; scalar() rejects on type before comparing content. The source states the hazard correctly: True == 1 and isinstance(True, int), so a schemaVersion of true compares equal to 1 under every naive test. Confirmed live: publishing rootBinding.schemaVersion as boolean true and a vector's `valid` as integer 0 are both rejected as SNV4-T.

perInstrument.subject: artifacts/r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.6.json
perInstrument.evidenceCategory: (b) re-runnable author-side evidence, with the parts anchored to live neighbour bytes the closest either instrument comes to (a), and the vector corpus at (c)
perInstrument.evidenceCategoryReasoning: Three distinct grades sit inside this instrument. FIRST, the arithmetic is real verification and not agreement: SHA-256 does not care who wrote the recipe, so recomputing every published digest from the published recordValue by two independently written encoders -- one table-driven, one flat imperative with hand-rolled big-endian -- and requiring them to agree with each other AND with the artifact is a measurement that can fail and does. The 720-value injectivity enumeration and the EXECUTED 554-byte falsifier are the same grade; the falsifier in particular is the strongest single artefact in either instrument, because it implements the REJECTED reading and demonstrates that a set-reading implementation mints PDD-01's identifier for PDD-17. SECOND, seven check functions read LIVE neighbour bytes -- v1.5, evaluation-proof.v8, c2-plan-stage-schema.v4 -- and rebuild values from them rather than from the subject. That is external anchoring the namespace instrument has none of, and it is the closest thing in this review to (a), though it is anchoring to a neighbour the same corpus produced, not to an independent derivation. THIRD, the recipe constants and the vector corpus are (c): the tags, namespace, domain and framing are declared in the checker and compared against the artifact's statement of them, and nothing outside either says 0x81 is the right tag for `variant`. CIR-B1 shows the vector corpus is (c) in a way that bites.
perInstrument.calibrationAnswer: How much of the green run is agreement rather than verification: for the ARITHMETIC, essentially none -- it is verification, because a wrong digest cannot survive recomputation regardless of who wrote the encoder. For the VECTOR CONTENT, most of it. I mutated a semantically load-bearing field in each vector and republished every digest with the instrument's own encoder: 6 of 17 vectors are anchored and reject (PDD-01..PDD-04 through fieldset/worked/equivalence/separation rebuilt from LIVE v1.5, and PDD-16/PDD-17 through the executed falsifier), and 11 of 17 accept any content the grammar admits. A malformed digest prefix `sha856:` passes. For the EXCEPTION MESSAGES the author's own concession is accurate: the 15 rejection controls are executed and each must raise on the condition it names with the exact message the artifact publishes, which proves the guard FIRES and proves the message is STABLE, but the message text itself is a string the checker and the artifact both carry, so its correctness is agreement. The instrument is right to execute them anyway -- section 7.2.2's rider is that a measurement which cannot fail the build is prose, and a guard that is asserted to raise on a named condition can fail.
perInstrument.whatWouldMoveItUp: The recipe is the hinge. Today the grammar is declared in the checker and the artifact's statement of it is compared against that declaration -- two statements of one reading. It would move to (a) if the recipe were re-derived from evaluation-proof.v8's normative preimage rules by a lane that had not read this artifact, and the published digests then recomputed from THAT derivation. The instrument already does the adjacent thing for the framing clauses, which it compares verbatim against live EP8 bytes, and for the field set, which it rebuilds from live v1.5 -- so the pattern is established and the remaining step is to extend it from the clauses to the tag assignments. Closing CIR-B1 does not change the category but it removes the gap between what the banner reads and what the run covers.

selftest.verifiedIndependently: mutation list enumerated and confirmed at 62 by importing the shipped module and calling _mutations(); coverage spans VECTOR, ORDER-RULING, TYPE, FALSIFIER, REJ, DECODER-PROBE, EQ, SEP, WORKED, RECIPE, GRAMMAR, EP8, ROUNDTRIP, POSTURE, PIN, PREDECESSOR, CARRY, SELFREPORT and FIELDSET

declaredMobileExemption.question: is the DECLARED_MOBILE exemption sound, or a hole?
declaredMobileExemption.ruling: SOUND, and better engineered than the question implies. It is not a hole.
reasoning: The permission is HARD-CODED in the checker as a two-element set and is not read from the artifact, so the artifact cannot widen it.
The artifact's own driftDisclosure is separately REQUIRED to name exactly those two documents, so the checker and the artifact must agree on the scope from opposite directions.
Widening from the artifact side is actively blocked: any other .md row whose name appears in the disclosure is reported as 'the disclosure names X, which is not declared mobile by this instrument'.

Neither mobile document is in PINS, so verified_snapshots() does not refuse on them -- the exemption is genuinely reachable rather than dead code behind an earlier refusal. I verified this by enumerating PINS (6 entries) and confirming neither mobile path is among them.
The drift is DISCLOSED, not absorbed: both documents are currently drifted and both lines print in the banner with recorded and live digests. I confirmed both are live-drifted right now.
Neither document's CONTENT is read for any assertion; they are hashed for the row comparison and nothing else. No published digest depends on them.
declaredMobileExemption.residual: The recorded digests of the two mobile rows are the only rows in frozenInputs not cross-checked against the checker's own PINS, because they are deliberately not pinned. A silent re-baseline of those two recorded values inside the artifact would therefore not be noticed. The practical impact is confined to the fidelity of the historical record -- what was current at authoring -- since no arithmetic depends on them. Recorded as CIR-NB-06, non-blocking.
declaredMobileExemption.verdictOnTheDesign: Disclosing drift rather than absorbing it is the correct treatment under freeze 7.2.1 rule 4, and hard-coding the permission on the checker side while requiring the artifact to name the same two documents is the right shape for an exemption. I would keep it.

well reasoned and the right call. Two independent encoders ARE run and compared on every record; the instrument reports its own count rather than asserting a number it did not produce. All five items are honestly stated and correctly scoped. The list is nevertheless INCOMPLETE: CIR-B1 is checkable, unchecked and unlisted. The failure is not misclassification, it is omission.

freezeComplianceInTheInstrumentItself.section75DuplicateKeyNamesTheKey: COMPLIANT. _pairs raises StrictJsonError('R1V16-JSON-DUPLICATE', f"duplicate object key {key!r}") so the duplicated key IS named, which is what section 7.5 requires and what it found 6 of 47 rejecting checkers failing to do. It names the key but not the path, where the namespace instrument names both; on this one point the namespace instrument is stronger. Both meet the requirement. Every JSON byte enters through a hooked parser -- strict_loads for the subject and v1.5, lenient_parse for two neighbours whose wire legitimately carries decimals -- and the lenient path still rejects duplicates and non-finites and still names the key.
freezeComplianceInTheInstrumentItself.section6Law18ExactType: COMPLIANT. check_law_eighteen tests `isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int)` for declared integer leaves, which rejects a boolean BEFORE admitting an integer -- the required bool-before-int ordering. The rationale is recorded and is correct: this class defeated C-2 at v3, v5, v6, v7 and v8 successively, each time inside the repair's own self-certification, and the section publishes every count as a JSON STRING precisely so that 17.0 and true cannot pass for 17. admit_record_value applies exact-type admission to every published recordValue BEFORE a single byte of it is encoded, and the declared-integer-leaf count is itself asserted against a constant declared in the checker rather than sized from the artifact.

escapesFound.summary: Ten of the seventeen published vectors collapse to byte-identical duplicates of PDD-01, carrying an identical derivationDigest, with 0 findings reported.

Nine inclusion controls can be neutralised in place -- the field each one exists to control is set back to PDD-01's value and the digests republished -- with 0 findings. An inclusion control that no longer differs is not reported as no longer controlling anything.

Eleven of seventeen vectors accept arbitrary same-length content in observationSetDigest, targetUniverseId and coverageContextDigest once the digests are republished with the instrument's own encoder. Even a malformed 'sha856:' prefix passes. This is calibration rather than a defect on its own -- these are synthetic controls whose absolute values are arbitrary by design -- but it bounds what a green run establishes about the corpus.

Thirteen of thirteen hand-written substring-preserving negations escape, covering all five properties, the observability boundary and the enforcement disclosure. Every required substring remains literally present and the meaning is reversed by appended or prepended prose.

escapesFound.summary: Swept over all 280 prose leaves of the effective contract longer than 25 characters: 63 positions are bound by containment (replacing the leaf is caught) yet accept a needle-preserving appended reversal with 0 findings. A further 41 positions are unbound entirely, giving 104 of 280 where an appended contradiction fires nothing.

falsePositivesFound.summary: Three of three lawful, meaning-preserving rewordings are rejected. Required-substring binding admits exactly one phrasing of each bound clause.
cases: SN-P4.ordering rewritten from 'The record precedes the namespace' to 'The namespace is created only after the record exists, never before.' -- identical meaning, rejected as SNV4-P4 statement omits 'The record precedes the namespace'

SN-P1.consumerConsequence rewritten to 'The authority record is the only thing that produces the root half of any canonical path.' -- identical meaning, rejected for omitting 'sole producer of the root half of every canonical path'

SN-P3.admissionCost rewritten with a clause reorder and 'content-addressed objects' spelled out -- identical meaning, rejected TWICE, for omitting both 'ranges over DIRECTORIES' and 'does not range over CAS objects'
falsePositivesFound.assessment: This is the known cost of the T13 technique and it is a real cost, not a theoretical one: a lawful successor that improves the prose of any of the 24 bound positions fails the build and its author must either revert the improvement or edit the checker. Measured brittleness: of 280 prose leaves, 239 are sensitive to wholesale replacement, and every one of the roughly 70 bound needles admits exactly one phrasing. The instrument does not disclose this.

falsePositivesFound.summary: policyDerivationIdentity.lawEighteenScope.rule rewritten from 'closed-scalar admission is exact-type.' to 'admission of closed scalars is exact-type.' -- identical meaning, rejected as R1V16-TYPE.
falsePositivesFound.assessment: R-1 binds prose by EXACT EQUALITY at 80 positions rather than by containment. That trade is the mirror image of the namespace instrument's: exact equality is immune to the negation attack that defeats containment, and is correspondingly 100 percent brittle to any rewording at every position it covers. Of the two, exact equality is the better choice for prose that is genuinely load-bearing, because a false positive is a build failure a human resolves in one edit while a false negative is a wrong artifact that ships green. Neither instrument discloses its prose-brittleness cost.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: Section 7.8 records 'each property gutted individually 13-18'. Measured range is 5-18. SN-P4 produces 5 findings and SN-P5 produces 6, roughly a third the binding density of SN-P2 at 18.
nonBlockingObservations.robustness: Stable across every gutting definition tested -- the shipped selftest's own _gut_properties, recursive leaf replacement preserving lists, and both keeping and discarding `title`. SN-P1=14, SN-P2=18, SN-P3=13, SN-P4=5, SN-P5=6 in all cases.

A signer reading '13-18' would take the binding to be roughly uniform across the five properties. It is not, and the two thinnest are the two that govern crash-time ordering.
nonBlockingObservations.action: correct the figure in section 7.8 to 5-18, or state the per-property vector. No status changes.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: The '133 findings on a gutted rootBinding' figure DOES reproduce, but it is definition-sensitive and the definition is recorded nowhere.
nonBlockingObservations.measurement: Swept 24 gutting definitions. 133 is produced by replacing every string leaf with a placeholder while PRESERVING list structure and leaving non-string scalars alone. Replacing list elements wholesale gives 126; emptying lists gives 111; collapsing lists to a single placeholder gives 119; placeholding non-string scalars too gives 134; using an empty string instead of a placeholder gives 108. Setting each top-level key of rootBinding to a placeholder gives 6.

nonBlockingObservations.action: record the gutting definition alongside the figure. The claim itself stands.

nonBlockingObservations.target: provenance of a quotation in circulation
nonBlockingObservations.finding: The concession attributed to the namespace instrument's author -- 'required-substring binding freezes prose', described as the known cost of T13's technique -- does not occur anywhere in this corpus.
nonBlockingObservations.method: whitespace-normalised search per freeze 7.7 across every .py, .json and .md file under docs/coop. 'freezes prose' 0 hits. "T13's technique" 0 hits. 'known cost' 1 hit, in plan-and-policy-identity-recipes.v2.json, on an unrelated subject.
nonBlockingObservations.whatIsActuallyThere: The nearest real text is threat-model-storage-namespace.v4.json's whyItWasDesignedToStayGreen, which states that each replaced prose value 'was written to preserve every substring T13 requires of it' -- that is the author explaining how the artifact stays green under the PREDECESSOR checker, not a concession about the successor instrument's brittleness. The quantified concession about this technique exists, but in a different lane's artifact: versioning-policy.v10.json, quoted in full under CIR-B2.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItMatters: The namespace instrument was reviewed partly on the understanding that its author had already conceded and scoped this limitation. The author did not. That is the gap CIR-B2 records.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: Neither instrument discloses its prose-binding cost in either direction. The namespace instrument does not say that containment admits a needle-preserving reversal; R-1 does not say that exact equality rejects a lawful rewording. Both costs are real and both were measured here (FP-01, FP-02, ESC-05, ESC-06).
nonBlockingObservations.precedent: versioning-policy.v10.json in this same corpus publishes exactly this class of boundary quantitatively and names the exact paths of each class rather than summarising. That is the standard already set here, and it is a good one.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: 407 of 930 string leaves longer than 25 characters (43 percent) accept a flat appended contradiction with 0 findings -- prose the instrument does not bind at all.
nonBlockingObservations.assessment: Not a defect on its own -- much of this is genuinely narrative, and binding narrative would multiply FP-02 across the artifact. It is reported because 57 percent coverage is the honest figure behind the phrase 'the reviewed values', and because several unbound positions are self-descriptive claims about the instrument's own discipline (parseDiscipline.rule, bindingDisclaimer.checkerCorpusUntouched) which a reader would reasonably expect to be bound.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: The two mobile rows' RECORDED digests are the only frozenInputs rows not cross-checked against the checker's own PINS, so a silent re-baseline of those two recorded values inside the artifact would not be noticed.
nonBlockingObservations.impact: Confined to the fidelity of the historical record. No published digest depends on either document and neither is read for content, so no arithmetic is affected. The exemption itself is sound -- see the perInstrument ruling.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: The subject publishes only counts for the shasum cross-check -- 47 byte strings, 0 mismatches -- and no digests and no byte strings, so there is nothing an instrument could recompute. '0 mismatches' remains an unverifiable attestation embedded inside an otherwise instrument-verified artifact.
nonBlockingObservations.assessment: The instrument is CORRECT to decline it and correct in its stated reason. Noted because it is the one place where the artifact could cheaply have converted an attestation into a check by publishing the 47 digests, and section 7.8's whole subject is that conversion.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: Both duplicate-key hooks name the duplicated key and both therefore comply. The namespace instrument additionally resolves and reports the PATH of each duplicate, handles duplicates inside objects the parse itself discarded, and retains live references so no id() can be reused by a collected object during path resolution. R-1 names the key only.
nonBlockingObservations.assessment: Compliance is not in question for either. Recorded because the namespace implementation is the better pattern and is worth carrying forward to successors.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: The instrument requires 720 enumerated SYNTHETIC values to produce 720 distinct encodings with 0 collisions, and requires no distinctness at all among the 17 PUBLISHED vectors. The distinctness discipline exists in the instrument and is applied to the corpus a reader never sees.
nonBlockingObservations.assessment: This is why CIR-B1 is a blocker rather than an accepted limitation: the capability is already present and is simply not pointed at the published corpus.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: The --subject entry point is honestly built: it prints R1V16-DIAGNOSTIC with the measured digest, states 'the subject pin was NOT enforced; this run is not a verdict', and returns a DISTINCT exit code 4 that cannot be confused with 0, 1, 2 or 3.
nonBlockingObservations.assessment: Commended. It made this review substantially easier to conduct without editing anything, and it is the right way to expose a checker to an adversary while keeping the verdict path pinned. The namespace instrument has no equivalent and I had to build a sandbox tree and re-pin a scratch copy to achieve the same thing.

nonBlockingObservations.finding: The instrument prints its own bound in its own banner: 'A green run is bounded author-side evidence; it is not acceptance, application, seal or qualification, and it closes no row.'
nonBlockingObservations.assessment: Accurate, and it is the correct reading. This review confirms that sentence by measurement rather than by agreement. The namespace instrument's banner carries the equivalent for its own scope -- 'this instrument changes no status, disposition, verdict or seal, and closes no row. TM remains UNSET - BLOCKS FREEZE.' Both are honest about standing; both are silent about coverage, which is what the two blockers address.

rulingOnTheApproach.question: is the companion-instrument approach sound?
rulingOnTheApproach.answer: YES, with the bound section 7.8 states, and this review adds a second bound section 7.8 does not state.
rulingOnTheApproach.section78ConfirmedByMeasurement: Section 7.8's central ruling is correct and I reached it independently rather than adopting it. A companion instrument converts an unverifiable attestation into a re-runnable check: both instruments can fail, both do fail on real defects, and both fail for stated reasons naming the position -- not merely by exiting non-zero. Section 7.2.2's rider is satisfied. And neither converts anything into independent evidence, because in each case the same reading produced both the artifact and the instrument, which I demonstrated concretely rather than inferred: the namespace instrument's prose half agrees with the artifact even when the artifact is reversed, and R-1's recipe constants have no referent outside the pair.
rulingOnTheApproach.theSecondBound: Section 7.8 grades these instruments on whether their assertions are LOAD-BEARING, and both authors proved that by showing findings fire when content is REMOVED. That is a necessary standard and it is the right one to have demanded. It is not sufficient, and the gap between the two standards is where both blockers live. Firing on ABSENCE and firing on FALSEHOOD are different properties. The namespace instrument fires on absence at 239 of 280 prose positions and on falsehood at 176 of them. R-1 fires on a wrong digest everywhere and on a vacuous control nowhere. A non-vacuity proof measures the first property, and section 7.8 currently reads as though it measured the second.
rulingOnTheApproach.whatANonVacuityProofShouldBe: The external-driver standard the namespace instrument set -- import the shipped file unmodified, mutate a copy, assert the SPECIFIC named family fires, and show separately that the pin refuses drifted bytes -- is the right standard and should be kept and required of successors. I reproduced all of it and endorse it. It should be EXTENDED by one requirement: for every assertion, exhibit an input that is WRONG rather than merely EMPTY, and record the positions where no such input could be constructed. That extension would have surfaced both blockers in this review at authoring time.
rulingOnTheApproach.whatASignerShouldReadAGreenRunAsMeaning: Section 7.8 already says: 'this artifact says what it says, consistently, and drift will be caught', never 'this artifact is right.' That is correct and a signer should keep it. This review sharpens the first clause. A green run means: (1) the pinned bytes are the reviewed bytes, and any drift in them or in their pinned inputs stops the run rather than re-baselining it -- this is fully earned and is the strongest thing either instrument delivers; (2) every value the artifact publishes that can be RECOMPUTED has been recomputed and agrees -- fully earned for R-1's digests and for the namespace instrument's vectors, operand pairs and closure counts; (3) the artifact's prose has not been GUTTED -- earned; and (4) NOT that the artifact's prose is not FALSE, and NOT that its published corpora are non-degenerate. A signer should read a green companion run as a strong statement about consistency and drift, a real statement about arithmetic, and no statement at all about truth.
rulingOnTheApproach.whatDischargesTheResidual: Unchanged and confirmed: an independent re-derivation, not more assertions from the same lane. This review is not that either -- it is an adversarial audit of two instruments, which bounds what they prove without proving the underlying claims. The residual stands.

This review's own file changes no finding of any class in that checker.

verifiedInputs.whatIWrote: exactly one file: docs/coop/artifacts/companion-instruments.review-independent.v1.json. No checker was edited, including the two under review. No other repository file was created, modified or deleted. All mutation work was done on copies under the session scratchpad, outside the repository.
verifiedInputs.techniqueDisclosure: Both instruments pin their subject's digest, so testing a mutated subject requires either the instrument's own unpinned diagnostic entry point or a re-pinned scratch copy of the checker. I used check-r1-v1.6.py's own --subject flag, which is unpinned by design and returns a distinct exit 4 declaring the run is not a verdict; and for the namespace instrument I built a sandbox tree outside the repository and re-pinned a SCRATCH COPY of the checker to the mutated subject digest. Re-pinning a scratch copy of the checker is a legitimate technique here, both instrument authors used it, and I state plainly that I did.

whatIDidNotCheck: The subject-matter correctness of either artifact. Both were independently reviewed ACCEPT with 0 blockers and this review does not reopen, revisit or rely on those verdicts. Every mutation was constructed to test the INSTRUMENT and no finding here is a finding against either subject.

An independent re-derivation of R-1's encoding recipe from evaluation-proof.v8's normative preimage rules. That is precisely the work that would move the recipe from category (c) to category (a), and not doing it is the main reason this review cannot upgrade R-1's grade. I verified the recipe is internally consistent and that the arithmetic over it is real; I did not verify the recipe is the right recipe.

EP8's 69-assertion framing gate -- the 12 record goldens and 9 commitment goldens re-encoded by a generic EP8-driven re-encoder. R-1's NOT_VERIFIED discloses that it does not re-run them and I did not re-run them either.

check-completeness.py, the namespace instrument's derivation reader, which is deliberately unpinned under freeze 7.6. I confirmed the derivation resolves to 1 addition, 0 removals and 12 changed prose leaves as the instrument requires, and that a broken reader could not fake that, but I did not audit the reader itself.
Cryptographic strength. I did not attempt collision or second-preimage constructions against either encoder, and the injectivity claims are taken as tested over the enumerated domain only.
The namespace instrument's SNV4-N non-interference family beyond the two mutations shipped for it, and SNV4-S scope beyond the closed-list mutation, the deletion case and the operations census.
Concurrency, filesystem race and TOCTOU behaviour of either instrument between hashing an input and reading it.

Whether the two DECLARED_MOBILE documents' current drift is itself lawful. I confirmed the drift is real, disclosed with both digests, and that no assertion depends on either document's content; I did not diff the documents or assess what changed in them.
The other companion instrument named in section 7.8, check-c2-v11.py. This review was scoped to the two instruments named in the task and says nothing about the third.
